key_insight: Constitutive-Set Mechanics replaces a single constitutive law with an admissible set and uses the structure’s own strain history to certify robust equilibrium responses and worst-case bounds.
engineering_relevance: This lets engineers quantify uncertainty in materials and models without choosing one fitted law too early, improving reliability for simulations of shells, fracture, and other load paths beyond available tests.
method: Formulate mechanics variationally over a set of admissible constitutive laws instead of one law.
Use the occupation measure of the reached strains to turn energy evaluation into a support-function problem.
Derive equilibrium-based certificates for robust upper bounds, with two-sided results under global minimization.
evidence_signal: The paper demonstrates the framework on linear elasticity, data-constrained constitutive functions, phase-field fracture, a finite-strain composite shell, and a membrane, with the shell probing only 4 of 226 constitutive directions and the membrane’s certified worst-case energy exceeding the reference by more than 4×.
watch_item: The approach depends on solving equilibrium problems and on a well-defined admissible constitutive set, so computational cost and the quality of the uncertainty description can limit practical use.
paper_title: Constitutive-Set Mechanics: variational mechanics on an admissible set of constitutive laws
